audit_findings.title: Partial-year Royston earnings and financing do not form a steady-state equity-OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: FY2026 equity OE is the forecast anchor, but it contains only post-March 24 Royston operations and acquisition interest while the balance sheet reflects the fully acquired business and debt.
audit_findings.evidence: Royston’s post-acquisition results of operations for the period from March 24, 2026, through June 30, 2026, are included in the Company’s Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The mixed-period anchor is demonstrated, although the resulting valuation error is not. Royston contributed $73.5 million of sales and $2.4 million of operating income during the partial period, while year-end debt was $255.931 million. A full year adds operating cash earnings, maintenance capex and working-capital needs but also adds interest expense. Because these omitted components work in opposite directions, the net effect is unresolved, but the scale of the acquisition makes it reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Build a same-perimeter annual equity-OE run rate using full-year Royston operating cash earnings, maintenance capex, working capital, integration costs and interest at current debt balances and rates; rerun every scenario and supersede it with the first full-year 10-K.

audit_findings.title: The bridge omits a $7.0 million earnout claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.044 million, equal to $0.18 per diluted share and 1.5% of the $471 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An unfunded contingent acquisition payment should reduce the equity bridge unless its cash cost is already captured once in forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has recorded a $ 7.0 million contingent liability related to the future earnout payments as part of the acquisition of Canada’s Best Holding (CBH), or which $ 2.1 million is classified as short term, while $ 4.9 million is classified as long term.
audit_findings.explanation: The omitted liability is a demonstrated bridge error if forecast OE does not already capture its settlement. Deducting the entire filed liability would reduce base equity value from $471.0 million to approximately $464.0 million and base value per share from $11.82 to about $11.65. That remains far below the $20.23 market price, so the maximum filed amount does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $3.690 million fair-value increase and the $7.044 million liability through reported earnings, operating cash flow and the OE calculation; then deduct the unfunded settlement once, including any supportable tax effect.

audit_findings.title: Royston accounting and controls were not yet seasoned
audit_findings.mechanism: Potential errors in Royston revenue, working capital, assumed liabilities or cash-flow classification could alter the OE anchor or equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our audit of, and opinion on, the Company’s internal control over financial reporting does not include the internal control over financial reporting of SRR Holdings, Inc. (“Royston”), a wholly-owned subsidiary, whose financial statements reflect total assets and revenues constituting 50 percent and 11 percent, respectively, of the related consolidated financial statement amounts as of and for the year ended June 30, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The control-scope exclusion is demonstrated, but no accounting error is demonstrated. The consolidated financial statements received an unqualified audit opinion, while Royston's internal controls were excluded from the ICFR opinion. Because Royston represented 50% of consolidated assets and 11% of annual revenue, an error could matter, but the record provides neither an identified misstatement nor a quantified exposure.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile Royston's post-close income and cash flow to audited subsidiary records, test revenue cut-off and acquired working-capital balances, and inspect the first full-year filing for control findings, purchase-accounting revisions and newly recognized liabilities.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may mix transaction one-offs with continuing integration costs
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.9 million, equal to 30.5% of the $32.5 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Classifying acquisition and integration spending as recurring or nonrecurring directly changes normalized anchor OE and therefore every projected year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company incurred acquisition-related costs totaling $ 9.9 million which are included in the selling and administrative expense line of the consolidated statements of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The $9.9 million expense is filed, but its treatment in the supplied OE calculation is not established. Leaving completed transaction fees in OE would understate value; removing continuing integration or operating costs would overstate value. The filing expressly says integration costs will continue, and the filed amount is nearly one-third of anchor OE, making the classification reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $9.9 million by invoice and activity to the FY2026 OE calculation, normalize only demonstrably completed transaction fees, retain continuing integration costs, apply tax effects once and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The acquisition working-capital settlement was unresolved at the bridge date
audit_findings.mechanism: The final purchase-price settlement may create a receivable that increases the equity bridge or a payable that reduces it; it should not enter operating OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The amount prefunded for cash and working capital will be adjusted in the first quarter of 2027 fiscal year to reflect the actual amounts acquired.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the $13.2 million prefunding was provisional, but it does not disclose the settlement difference or its direction. Consequently, a bridge adjustment may be required, but present materiality cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the fiscal-2027 first-quarter settlement statement and cash payment or receipt, then adjust the bridge by the final difference without recording it as operating OE.

audit_findings.title: All balance-sheet cash was added without establishing that it was excess
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $14.249 million, equal to $0.36 per diluted share and 3.0% of the $471 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash needed for operations or covenant liquidity supports OE and should not also be added as a distributable non-operating asset in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company considers our level of cash on hand, borrowing capacity, current ratio and working capital levels to be our most important measures of short-term liquidity.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation demonstrably adds all cash, while the filing describes cash as an important liquidity measure rather than establishing it as surplus. Nevertheless, even treating none of the $14.249 million as excess would reduce base equity value to about $456.8 million and base value per share to about $11.46, still well below the $20.23 market price. The maximum possible correction therefore does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Estimate minimum operating, seasonal and covenant cash after the acquisition and replace the $14.249 million bridge addition with only the demonstrably unrestricted surplus amount.
